name: Robust Recovery

currentBonuses.when: on saves against a disease or poison after you Treat a Disease/Poison, or someone with this feat treats you

corrections.problem: The condition is invented and mis-attributed. The record says: "When you Treat a Disease or a Poison, or someone else uses one of these actions on you, increase the circumstance bonus granted on a success to +4". The spec's `when` reads "...or someone with this feat treats you" — the text imposes NO requirement that the treater have the feat (the feat is yours; any treater's success gives you +4). The other half is also wrong on your own sheet: when YOU Treat a Disease/Poison on an ally, the improved +2→+4 goes to the PATIENT, not to you, so "after you Treat a Disease/Poison" should not appear as a condition on your own save unless you treated yourself. Confirmed identical wording in the AoN mirror (feat-5207.json / feat-836.json).

Add an engineNote: when you use Treat a Disease/Poison on an ALLY, the improved bonus lands on the ally and is not representable; the success→critical success upgrade is a degree-of-success change with no representation.

corrections.problem: The condition is misstated in a way that inverts who needs the feat, and it silently merges a branch that does not apply to you. The record reads: "When you Treat a Disease or a Poison, or someone else uses one of these actions on you, increase the circumstance bonus granted on a success to +4". The spec's `when` says "...or someone with this feat treats you" — the text imposes no such requirement on the treater. YOUR feat upgrades the bonus YOU receive from anyone's treatment. Conversely, the other branch ("when you Treat a Disease or a Poison") upgrades the bonus for the PATIENT you treated, i.e. another character — so it is not self-applicable at all and must not be part of the condition on your own save star.

Replace the `when` with: "on saves against a disease or poison you were Treated for — whenever anyone uses Treat a Disease or Treat a Poison on you (your feat raises the bonus from +2 to +4)". The archetype's real mask gate is the separate clause 'if another creature ever learns your true face or name, you lose your abilities from this archetype', which is an archetype-loss rule, not a per-save condition.

corrections.problem: A second bonus in the record is missing. If you have the Sow Rumor feat, you can have your admirers assist you, with the same benefits as Gather Information." name: Don thy Fervor

for 1 minute after you activate Don thy Fervor
for 1 minute after you activate Don thy Fervor

corrections.problem: WRONG TARGET on the 4th entry. The record's text is: "you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, and Intimidation skill checks. In addition, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to counteract checks." The spec parks the counteract bonus on targetKind 'spell' and calls it "an approximation". This feat grants NO bonus to spell attack rolls and NO bonus to spell DC, so whichever of those the 'spell' target resolves to, the sheet will display a +2/+3 the character does not have — the exact failure mode the brief calls out ("a +1 to Athletics to Climb recorded as a generic bonus"). The brief also says: when the app has no stat for a bonus, set needsEngineWork and say what is missing — not to attach it to the nearest wrong stat. (The three skill entries are exact and should stay.)
corrections.correction: Drop the 'spell' entry from bonuses. Keep only skill/deception, skill/diplomacy, skill/intimidation, each "+2 circumstance (+3 at 18th level)" / when "for 1 minute after you activate Don thy Fervor". Keep needsEngineWork true with the note: "counteract checks have no stat in the app; the +2/+3 circumstance bonus to counteract checks cannot be represented and is deliberately not attached to any existing target." Note this is the opposite call from cardinal-guardians, where the text really does say "spell attack modifier" — that one legitimately belongs on a spell-attack target once attack-vs-DC is separated.

name: Acupuncturist

currentBonuses.bonus: +1 circumstance (+2 on a critical success; –1 penalty to all downtime skill checks on a critical failure)

corrections.problem: CONDITION BROADENED (minor). The record says the critical success grants "your ally the choice of a +2 circumstance bonus to one downtime activity skill check within the next week, OR the ability to roll twice on their next saving throw ... against an affliction". The spec's two entries read as if a critical success grants both: entry 1 says "+2 on a critical success" and entry 2 says "critical success only" with no indication they are mutually exclusive.

Everything else in this spec is accurate: all effects land on the ally ("You spend a day studying an ally"), so needsEngineWork true and no star on the feat holder's own stats is the right call.

corrections.problem: The AC condition is broadened past what the text supports, and it is marked confidence:high / needsHumanDecision:false. The record reads "gaining a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and to saving throws against spells that target you" — the trailing clause "against spells that target you" can grammatically attach to BOTH the AC and the saves, and its own successor feat (Preternatural Parry, which lists Spell Parry as a prerequisite) restricts both halves to the triggering effect. The spec asserts the AC half "applies to everything while the guard is up", which is one reading, not the text.

The clause placement is ambiguous and the app owner should pick the ruling." Until then phrase the AC `when` as "until the start of your next turn after using Spell Parry, as long as you keep a hand free (GM call whether the AC half is limited to spells that target you)". Downgrade confidence to medium.

The engineer silently repaired the record while quoting it, which breaks the 'ground it in the record's own text' rule and hides a genuine data defect.
corrections.correction: Verdict (situational:false, no tracked-stat bonus) is correct and stands. Replace the evidence with the literal string "its target takes 1d6. Your eidolon gains an item bonus to this bleed damage equal to the unarmed attack's item bonus to attack rolls. This is a critical specialization effect." and add to the engineNote: core.json's Bloodletting Claws description is truncated — the printed feat is 1d6 persistent bleed damage, so this record needs a data fix in the importer/description lane (separate from, and in addition to, the missing critSpec flag the spec already noted).

corrections.problem: The `evidence` is not the record's text. core.json actually reads "...its target takes 1d6. Your eidolon gains an item bonus to this bleed damage equal to the unarmed attack's item bonus to attack rolls. This is a critical specialization effect." — the damage type is MISSING entirely ("takes 1d6."); the spec silently supplied it as "1d6 [persistent bleed]". The task's ground-in-the-record rule was broken, and the real finding (an importer data defect in core.json) was masked as a normal quote.

Fix the evidence to the literal text and raise a separate data bug: bloodletting-claws' description lost its "persistent bleed" damage type in core.json.

name: Cobra Stance

currentBonuses.when: while you are in Cobra Stance (also applies to your Fortitude DC); Cobra Envenom raises this to +2

corrections.problem: The +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves is ALREADY folded into the computed total by the engine, so a feat-keyed situational entry double-reports it. core.json stances['cobra-stance'] carries saves.fortitude {value:1,type:'circumstance'}, and derive.ts:172-173 reads it ("The active stance/form may grant a save bonus (Cobra Stance: +1 Fortitude), typed so it pools") whenever the stance is active. The spec's own engineNote spots the stance data but then concludes the star "covers it in practice" — it does not: the player would see +1 already inside the Fortitude number AND a star claiming +1, and because the registry is keyed on the FEAT id the star would light merely because the feat is owned, even out of stance.

name: Dragon Roar

currentBonuses.when: on your first attack that hits a creature frightened by your Dragon Roar, before the end of your next turn (requires Dragon Stance)

corrections.problem: The condition is narrower than the text. core.json reads "Your first attack that hits a frightened creature after you roar and before the end of your next turn gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage" — ANY frightened creature. The spec's `when` says "against a creature frightened by your Dragon Roar", which would tell a player at the table they lose the bonus against a creature frightened by an ally's Demoralize, when in fact they get it.
corrections.correction: Rephrase to: "on your first attack that hits a frightened creature after you Dragon Roar, before the end of your next turn (requires Dragon Stance; the effect ends immediately if you leave Dragon Stance)". Bonus (+4 circumstance) and target (strikeDamage) are correct.

corrections.problem: CONDITION NARROWED beyond the text. The record says: "Your first attack that hits a frightened creature after you roar and before the end of your next turn gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage." It says A FRIGHTENED CREATURE — any frightened creature. The spec's `when` restricts it to "a creature frightened by your Dragon Roar", which is an invented narrowing. A player reading the app's condition would wrongly forgo the +4 against a foe frightened by an ally's Demoralize, by Dread Marshal Stance, by a spell, or by an earlier roar's lingering frightened value.
corrections.correction: Keep situational:true, targetKind strikeDamage, +4 circumstance. Rewrite the condition to: "on the first attack that hits a frightened creature (any source of frightened) after you Roar, before the end of your next turn; requires Dragon Stance, and the effect ends immediately if you leave Dragon Stance". The stance-exit clause ("Its effects end immediately if you leave Dragon Stance") is also missing from the spec and is worth keeping in the player-facing text.
